To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
we determined the molecular interface of the HIV-1 trans-activator protein Tat with the importin-α nuclear import receptor.
the HIV- 1 Tat protein binds to the nuclear import receptor importins via a mechanism distinct from other viruses, such as Ebola.

the HIV- Tat:NLS/CPR region forms a direct and stable interaction with importin-α, and that the binding interface is the same region that is also used for host factors such as the Ku70 and Ku70 proteins.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the molecular mechanism of HIV-1 Tat importin-α interaction, which may provide a target for the design of new therapeutic agents to combat HIV-1 infection.
the mechanism by which HIV-1 Tat enters the nucleus of the cell and the molecular basis for this process.
the structural basis for the interaction of Tat with importin-α, and the molecular determinants that are required to mediate the interaction.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
HIV-1 Tat binds importin-α in a similar manner to other host factors.
the Tat NLS/CPP binds importin-α in a similar fashion to the host protein Ku70, and this interaction is likely to be a conserved feature of Tat proteins from other retroviruses.
Tat:NLS/CPR binds importin-α through a similar mechanism to host factors.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the HIV- 1 Tat NLS/CPP binds to importin-α via an identical interface to host proteins, and that the Tat NLS/CPR is able to compete with host proteins such as Ku70/80.

we have determined the structure of the Tat:NLS/CPI binding to the classical nuclear import factor, importin-α, and that this binding is similar to that of other cellular factors such as Ku, but distinct from viral factors such as Ebola VP40.
HIV-1 Tat uses the same importin-α binding site as host proteins such as Ku70/80 and the Tat:NLS/CPR region is able to bind importin-α with a similar binding affinity.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the HIV- 1 Tat:NLS binds to importin-α in the same manner as host proteins.
the HIV- 1 Tat:NLS/ CPP is a potent inhibitor of nuclear import of host factors and that the Tat protein has evolved to mimic the host nuclear import machinery.
the Tat:NLS/CPR region binds importin-α in a manner that is distinct from other viral proteins, which may be a mechanism for the virus to avoid immune surveillance.
